properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): reflow2's served text describes one deployment, a local store the agent's person owns on the server's own machine, and is byte-identical on a registry-served (hosted) engine. A hosting layer then changes the rules under it (approver bound by the host, no tracked export, files never opened) with no way to say so, and the nudge sentence reports the HOST's setup as "this project"
properties.statement:
① OBSERVED. Two items in art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, both from the StoryFlow design's first sessions on api.flo2.io (reflow2 0.72.0 behind flo2's gateway):
(D1) set_decision_status with `approver` was refused three times, although add_decision says approver is "REQUIRED when the status is past the landing default" and set_decision_status says `deferred` "wants `approver`".
(D2) Nothing told the session whether an export was still owed.
Expected: served text that is true where it is served. NOT affected: reflow2 behaves correctly on a local store.

② PRECEDENT, searched. fact:defect-claim-region-describes-an-architecture-it-is-not-running (2026-08-07, reported three times): claim_region's description asserts that "the design lives as a file in each checkout with no shared server (dec:multi-writer-architecture)", and the fix shape recorded then was "make the description architecture-neutral or deployment-aware". MEASURED TODAY: 0.72.0 still serves that sentence, 52 days later and a day after dec:multi-writer-architecture was superseded. The instance was never fixed, and neither was the class.

③ CANDIDATES. (a) The served text has no deployment input. It is compiled per tool for a local store, and there is no channel for a host to amend a description. What reflow2 offers is per-design lessons through `steps`, the --remote client's handshake notice (proxy.rs with_notice), and per-request `_meta` writes_for, which is attribution only. (b) The host alone is at fault: flo2 changed the rules and could amend the text (it already rewrites 4 schemas and puts a preamble in front of the handshake). (c) The text is merely stale: it predates the 2026-09-27 design-and-export rules, and a one-time rewrite fixes it. (d) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: a hosted engine already serves different text.

④ WHAT WOULD TELL THEM APART. (d) predicts local and registry text differ. (c) predicts the contradicted claims are all export- or git-era. (b) alone predicts that every false claim traces to a rule flo2 introduced. (a) predicts identical text, and false claims from several unrelated rules, including some no host introduced.

⑤ RESULT (0.72.0 binary, scratch stores, 2026-09-28).
- The handshake instructions (8,065 chars), tools/list (193 tools: descriptions and schemas) and get_instructions are byte-identical under `--graph-path … --http` and under `--registry-root … --http` at /g/<id>/mcp.
- The handshake's nudge sentence is measured on the SERVER's machine. The same registry design said `installed` under the server's own HOME, and "REFLOW2 HAS NOT INSTALLED A SESSION-END NUDGE in this project" under an empty HOME. So on flo2, a person's agent is told about "this project" from what flo2's container has installed; that sentence appears in this hub's own flo2 design instructions.

A bounded sweep covered 185 tools, 31 skills, the handshake and get_instructions. The 185 are the tools api.flo2.io offers; api.flo2.io refuses 8 of reflow2's 193.
- APPROVER. All 8 tools that take an approver describe it as the Contributor the caller names (acknowledge_defect, acknowledge_gap, acknowledge_gaps, add_decision, add_design_rule, add_requirement, set_decision_status, set_requirement_status). The constructors call it REQUIRED past proposed. 6 skills say to pass it as "the Contributor whose word it is": capture-intent, establish-taxonomy, governance-proposal, kpp-proposal, revise-design and why. The door refuses every name except the caller's own flo2 id (recorded in flo2's design, fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28).
- LOCAL STORE AND EXPORTS. get_instructions' restore section names `.reflow2/graph`, `--graph-path … --stop-shared` and `--import`, and it says "the graph against the committed export (compare_designs)", but api.flo2.io refuses compare_designs. loop_status's only export sentence is "export before you finish"; see fact:root-cause-a-hosted-session-hears-nothing-about-exports-because-the-only-export-line-rides-a-tracked-export-2026-09-28. The skills ci-gate, parallel-work, revise-design, help and report-friction name local paths or exports.
- MEASURED ON DISK. link_artifact, reconcile_artifacts and set_artifact_checksum(s) describe the server measuring under the project root. The door refuses them unless the caller brings the evidence.
- TOOLS THE DOOR REFUSES. They are named as next steps in 8 tool descriptions and 5 skills.
- writes_for is answered by flo2, never by reflow2.
In all, a pattern sweep (not read line by line) found 38 of 218 units carrying at least one claim the hosted door contradicts.

Verdicts. (d) REFUTED. (c) PARTIAL: approver, nudge and writes_for are not export- or git-era claims. (b) PARTIAL: the nudge sentence and the claim_region sentence are false on a hosted engine with no flo2 rule involved. (a) CONFIRMED.

⑥ CLASS. reflow2's served text describes one deployment: a local store owned by the agent's person, on the machine the server runs on. A hosting layer then changes the rules without the text changing. That layer can be flo2's door or reflow2's own registry mode. reflow2 knows when it is registry-served and reads that in exactly one answer, and nothing lets a host declare which rules it changed. Fixing instances has not closed the class: the claim_region instance was reported three times, recorded with its fix shape, and still ships. Would a fix to the approver text alone have stopped the claim_region or nudge reports? No. So the cause is the missing deployment input, not any single sentence.

⑦ Out of scope. A class-pinning test would assert two things, generated from the served surface rather than from a hand-kept list:
(i) for a design served without its tree (a registry), no served text instructs a local-store operation (`.reflow2/graph`, `--graph-path`, "export before you finish") or makes a claim about "this project" measured on the host, unless it says it is local-only;
(ii) a contract change a host declares (for example "approver is bound by the host") reaches every tool whose schema carries the affected argument, driven by the schema the way flo2's bindApprovals is.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. The sweep's patterns over- and under-count, so 38 is an order of magnitude, not a census. Only D1 and D2 are observed to have misled an agent; the other claims are contradicted on paper. Whether a host-amendment channel belongs in reflow2 at all, or only at flo2's door, is open (dec:idea-tool-descriptions-match-the-hosted-door).

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. "The tool descriptions should say what the hosted server actually expects" HELD, as one instance of this class. "The export rule has an unclear future on a hosted graph" HELD, as another.
